findings.F1: Up streaks keep going, and more so the longer they are: each extra consecutive up close adds +0.28 % to the coin's excess 2-day return (slope t 2.74 with each day's cases taken together, 3666 cases on 971 days); up streaks of 5 or more days are followed by +0.99 % (t 2.23, 182 cases) and a single up day by -0.32 % (t -2.28, 1966 cases), while down-streak length grades nothing (t 0.33, 3536 cases, 940 days).
findings.F2: The rebound after a fall grows with the coin's volatility: per unit of fall in usual moves, the slope is 0.36 % in the coin's lowest 60-day-volatility tercile (t 1.50, 487 days), 0.56 % in the middle (t 1.41, 556 days) and 1.34 % in the highest (t 1.97, 528 days); measured on the raw percentage fall, the slope is 0.20 per unit of return (t 2.40, 940 days), above the tested vol-scaled forecast's 2.28.
findings.F3: The rebound is in the 2-day horizon only: falls of 0.75 to 1.5 usual moves are followed by +0.80 % over 2 days (t 3.07, 847 cases), but over 5 days the fall slope is 0.21 % (t 0.35, 406 days) and that bucket is -0.38 % (t -0.82).
findings.F4: The book's gain is defensive rather than timed: it beat holding in the falling years (2018 -0.12 % against -0.35 % a day, 2022 -0.03 % against -0.19 %) and trailed it in every strong year (2020 +0.21 % against +0.42 %, 2021 +0.14 % against +0.41 %, 2024 +0.07 % against +0.24 %, 2025 +0.06 % against +0.20 %).
findings.F5: Weekday effects do not stand out once each day's cases are taken together: Friday's next-day excess of +0.30 % has t 2.09 (414 days), but only t 1.61 and 1.37 in the two halves of the period, and no other weekday reaches |t| 1.6. This is chance among the many angles looked at.

ideas.idea: The more consecutive days a coin has closed higher, the more it rises over the next 2 days beyond its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader should hold onto, not fade, a coin that has strung together a long run of up closes, expecting a short further rise that is larger the longer the run.
ideas.name: long up streaks keep rising

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's percentage fall on its latest day, the more it rises over the next 2 days, and this rebound is larger the higher the coin's volatility over the past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying the dip should expect the largest short rebounds after big falls in turbulent periods and little after falls in calm ones, which makes the bet worth its cost mainly when volatility is high.
ideas.name: volatile falls rebound harder
